findings.claim: Listing users with order counts performs a full scan of all orders for every user, giving O(users × orders) work and causing CPU and response-time growth that can make the operation unusable on production-sized datasets.
evidence: evals/cases/case_08/src/users.py:15-16 loops over every user and invokes orders_for_user once per user.
evals/cases/case_08/src/users.py:9-10 implements each orders_for_user invocation by iterating through the entire _orders collection.
A runtime probe with 40 users and 250 instrumented orders observed exactly 10,000 user_id reads (40 × 250), while producing the correct aggregate count of 250 orders; the scoped test also passed.
